nodes.id: Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation

analysis.research_problem: The paper aims to improve the effectiveness, efficiency, and economy of LLM-based Text-to-SQL solutions.
analysis.technique: The paper proposes a new integrated solution, DAIL-SQL, based on a systematic comparison of prompt engineering methods, including question representation, example selection, and example organization.
analysis.evaluation_result: The paper introduces DAIL-SQL, an integrated solution that achieves an execution accuracy of 86.6% on the Spider leaderboard.
analysis.research_gap: The paper addresses the absence of a systematic benchmark for evaluating LLM-based Text-to-SQL solutions and token efficiency in prompt engineering.
analysis.limitation_scope: The paper explores the potential of open-source LLMs and the advantages/disadvantages of supervised fine-tuning.
analysis.modulesComponents: Prompt Engineering (Question Representation, Example Selection, Example Organization), Supervised Fine-tuning
analysis.challenges: Token efficiency in prompts, lack of systematic benchmarks.
analysis.limitationsOpenProblems: High cost and token limits of proprietary LLMs; performance gap in open-source LLMs.

nodes.id: DIN-SQL: Decomposed In-Context Learning of Text-to-SQL with Self-Correction

analysis.research_problem: The paper addresses the problem of improving the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the reasoning process for the text-to-SQL task.
analysis.technique: The core technique involves decomposing the text-to-SQL task into smaller sub-tasks and feeding the solutions of these sub-tasks into LLMs to improve performance.
analysis.evaluation_result: The proposed approach improves performance in text-to-SQL tasks, achieving an execution accuracy of 85.3% on the Spider holdout test set, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art. It also achieved an execution accuracy of 55.9% on the BIRD benchmark, setting a new state-of-the-art.
analysis.research_gap: There is a significant gap between the performance of fine-tuned models and prompting approaches using Large Language Models (LLMs) on the text-to-SQL task.
analysis.limitation_scope: The abstract does not explicitly mention the limitations or future work, but it suggests the approach is more effective than fine-tuning, indicating a potential area for further investigation into the trade-offs between prompting and fine-tuning.
analysis.modulesComponents: Schema Linking, Query Decomposition, SQL Generation, Self-Correction
analysis.challenges: Improving reasoning capabilities of LLMs for complex queries.
analysis.limitationsOpenProblems: Generalizability to other complex reasoning tasks.
analysis.applicationsUseCases: Natural language database querying, complex reasoning tasks.
